topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer causes and carcinogenicity, and establishes the scope of the session.

topics.label: Biological Nature and Origins of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by the accumulation of mutations from endogenous cellular processes and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Carcinogens and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the contribution of external exposures to cancer development through common environmental carcinogens, the debate over random chance, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how viral and bacterial pathogens contribute to malignancy, exemplified by the interaction between malaria and Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical agents, often following metabolic activation by endogenous enzymes, inflict direct DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Host Susceptibility Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how non-mutagenic environmental and host conditions drive tumor progression by promoting the proliferation of initiated cells.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the laboratory and epidemiological strategies used to identify carcinogens and establish their causal links to cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within everyday risk-benefit decisions and summarizing the main takeaways.
